A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EPPO study. All 22 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including derivations, experimental details, tables and learning-curve appendices, support comparison despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Ant and HalfCheetah simulations under changing friction and joint torque, with return statistics and learning curves averaged over ten seeds.

after.justification: v2 reports original results for the same non-stationary control experiments, with updated return statistics and learning curves averaged over 15 seeds.

M1.justification: The evidential critic, hyperprior-regularized objective and UCB update remain unchanged. EPPOmean, EPPOcor and EPPOind are all retained; v2 presents EPPOmean as a control rather than one of three proposed variants. The corrected expectation formula does not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 14 MuJoCo-v5 scenarios: four slippery configurations and ten paralysis configurations across Ant and HalfCheetah. Friction ranges, torque schedules and affected joints match, including the appendices.

E2.justification: PPO and PFO remain the evaluated baselines in every corresponding experiment, alongside the same three EPPO variants. The generic baseline labels in v2 Figure 1 refer to existing methods, and the detailed comparisons retain their membership.

E3.justification: Both retain 500,000 training steps per task, the same network sizes and hyperparameters, the same confidence-radius selection procedure, evaluation every 20,000 steps with ten episodes, and AULC/final-return metrics. The changed repetition count belongs to E5; hardware and timing are newly documented.

E4.justification: Both assess optimism through the EPPOmean/cor/ind comparison under the same friction and paralysis changes. The revised introduction plot redisplays an existing HalfCheetah experiment. No new ablation, sensitivity, calibration or robustness study is presented.

E5.justification: Reported repetitions increase from ten seeds, 1-10, to 15 seeds, 1-15, throughout the results and appendix settings. Both already report means with standard errors and one-standard-error shading; the uncertainty-reporting procedure is otherwise retained.

E6.justification: The numerical evidence is extensively updated for the expanded run set in v1 Tables 4-5 versus v2 Tables 1-2 and the learning curves. For example, slippery AULC average ranks change from 2.0 to 1.5 for EPPOcor and from 1.5 to 1.8 for EPPOind, reversing their rank ordering. v2 also adds runtime totals and omits v1's combined overall summary.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the temporal-difference expectation from r_t + gamma E[V_t] to r_t + gamma E[V_{t+1}] - E[V_t], restoring consistency with the earlier TD definition. v2 also explicitly specifies time-dependent transitions and time-homogeneous rewards. The appendix derivations are retained.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contribution on overfitting as the primary cause of plasticity loss and evidential regularization as the remedy. v2 instead centers a two-part hypothesis: value uncertainty preserves critic plasticity through detecting distribution shifts and enables directed exploration. The broad empirical superiority claim remains.

C2.justification: v2 introduces an uncertainty-to-training-loss explanation for maintaining plasticity and changes EPPOind's interpretation from more myopic to more far-sighted. Section 5 adds substantive limitations concerning uncertainty calibration, convergence analysis and reliance on one physics engine. v1's off-policy/offline applicability discussion is removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds hardware specifications, parallel-execution information and per-method wall-clock totals in Section 4, plus a promise to release the implementation upon acceptance in Appendix B.2. It also makes the PPO value-target description more explicit. Most implementation and hyperparameter details were already present in v1.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions the work around directed exploration and non-stationary adaptation, adding discussion of Wang et al. (2019), Zhang et al. (2022), and model-based reactive exploration by Steinparz et al. (2022), plus bandit and newer plasticity literature. It removes the off-policy/offline extension discussion and associated references.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around a highlighted hypothesis. Background and method explanations are revised, experimental subsections are reorganized, and the conclusion is replaced by a limitations-and-broader-impact section. Appendix organization and terminology also change.

P2.justification: The main empirical presentation is reorganized: v1's aggregate Table 1 is removed, while appendix Tables 4-5 become main-text Tables 1-2. The illustrative learning curve becomes introduction Figure 1, shortened from 4.5 to 2 million steps with four relabeled curves. Figure placement, table placement and document layout are extensively reflowed.

improvement.justification: The additional repetitions, corrected TD expectation, resource disclosure and explicit calibration, convergence and domain limitations improve precision and transparency. Moving detailed results into the main text also aids scrutiny. The method and experimental coverage remain stable, and the new uncertainty-driven plasticity mechanism lacks direct diagnostic validation, so the overall gain is limited.
